_note: SAMPLE. Generated from the hypothesised draft so the pages can be built and reviewed before Thursday. Replaced by live data on draft day.

roast.text: Keshia took the best player on the board with the third pick of the draft, which is the correct outcome arrived at by unclear means. No one else had taken a quarterback yet, so she did not out-think anyone; she simply sat down first at a table that was already set. We are logging it as competence and reserving the right to revise.

Three running backs came off the board and Jay watched all three, thought hard, and then did the fourth-most original thing available. Jonathan Taylor went within a third of a pick of his national average, which means Jay did not draft so much as ratify. Somewhere a consensus board sighed with relief.

Justin let the receiver run start without him, waited for two other people to do the thinking, and then took the guy the entire country had already agreed on, roughly a pick and a half after they would have. Correct pick, no fingerprints on it. Substation Superstars are currently one for one on decisions made by process of elimination.

Mike wanted Jalen Hurts and nobody in this room was going to stop him, so he beat a field of zero competitors by six picks. James Cook III was sitting right there and lasted exactly one more selection. Mike bid against himself, overpaid, and looked pleased about it.

Evan took James Cook III one pick after he was already the highest-ranked man alive, which required him to do nothing but not stand up. His team name is still "Waiting to draft...", which is either an oversight or the most honest self-assessment in the league. This was the pick a coin flip would have made.

For Chris Olave in round two to work, Bree needs a career year, needs thirty better players to quietly underperform, and needs Breece Hall to have never existed. She has two receivers and a plan that requires the rest of the league to cooperate. Nobody has agreed to this.

Jesse needed a second running back and needed him badly enough to walk past fourteen better options, one of whom was Ashton Jeanty. He now has two running backs and the smug air of a man who thinks he has beaten the market to something. Mr. Anderson is drafting like the board owes him money.

Chenell read that Nico Collins is expected to lead the Texans receiving corps after Jayden Higgins's season-ending ACL tear and treated it as classified intelligence. She then paid for it by stepping over CeeDee Lamb, who was the twenty-fourth-best player available and is not a secret. Da Reigning Champ is defending the title on scoops everyone else also read.
3 of the last 5 picks were QBs, and Evan jumped in for Patrick Mahomes.

Mike now has four quarterbacks and nothing else. Not a running back, not a receiver, not a single человек who catches a ball. He took Jaxson Dart, part of a Giants trio that played eighteen snaps together in 2025, to be the fourth man in a room where two of them can start and the other two watch Mike watch them.

For Tetairoa McMillan here to work, Colin needs eighteen better players to collectively forget how to play, needs Justin Herbert to have been a rumor, and needs Drake London to file for retirement quietly. He has two backs, two receivers, and a board he is treating as a suggestion. 4th and Inshes is a plan held together by other people failing.

Keshia has now taken four quarterbacks in a league that starts a small fraction of that, and this is the one where she accidentally landed the best player left on the board. Three of her last five picks have been quarterbacks, so the correct pick arrived purely because she was already standing in that aisle. Competence by saturation: throw enough darts at one wall and one of them is bound to hit the target.

Jordan Love sat there being the fifty-fourth best player alive while Tyler went shopping twenty-nine spots down the shelf for DJ Moore. That is three receivers in his last five picks, which means Tyler is not drafting a team, he is completing a collection. Somebody should tell him the league does not award points for theme.

Justin has now built a roster with two quarterbacks, one running back, one receiver and a tight end, which is not a lineup so much as a sampler platter. He stepped over George Pickens to add Harold Fannin Jr., meaning the process-of-elimination era is officially over and the guessing era has begun. Substation Superstars have moved from having no fingerprints on their picks to having them all over the wrong ones.

Colin took Tony Pollard twenty-five picks before the rest of the country had any intention of doing so, which is less a draft strategy than a solo expedition. Zay Flowers, DeVonta Smith and George Kittle all watched him walk past. He now has three running backs and the settled look of a man who has stopped consulting anything.

Bree wanted a second quarterback and wanted him so badly that George Kittle, the sixty-third best player breathing, was simply furniture. Her plan already required thirty better players to underperform; now it requires Sam Darnold to be one of the reasons why. Three receivers, two tight ends, and a league that still has not agreed to any of this.

Doug now has five running backs, one receiver and a quarterback, which means every Sunday he will start three of them and explain to the other two that it is nothing personal. Bhayshul Tuten was genuinely the best man left, so the pick is fine; the shape around it is a man building a relay team and entering a football league. Somewhere in Doug's house there is a roster page he has scrolled past sideways.

For this to work, Chenell needs Sam LaPorta to disappear, needs twenty-one better players to sit down, and needs DK Metcalf's questionable designation to resolve in her favor. She is now defending a title on secondhand scoops and optimism about a medical report. Da Reigning Champ has moved from reading the news to hoping it changes.

Tyler has two quarterbacks and five receivers. No running backs. Not one. He has assembled a passing offense with nobody to hand the ball to and no way to stop handing it, and the second half of this draft is going to look like a supply run.

James drafted Luther Burden III with the confidence of a man remembering highlights that have not been filmed yet. Burden suffered a groin injury on 8 August in a contested red-zone rep, and James looked at that and reached eleven spots past Rome Odunze anyway. Three receivers now, all of them purchased on a memory.

Justin took Rome Odunze with nobody better on the board, which after the guessing era arrives as a genuine shock. There was nothing to eliminate, nothing to guess at, and no way to get this wrong, so he didn't. Substation Superstars have finally made a correct pick, and the only explanation available is that the board ran out of chances to trip him.

Tee Higgins was the last obvious name on the board and Mike walked up and took him like a man collecting a parcel. Five quarterbacks, one running back, one receiver: he has spent this draft assembling the most eccentric roster in the league and then, at the one moment courage was free, did exactly what everyone would have. The quarterback room is now large enough that Higgins can throw to himself and still be outnumbered.

Evan has one quarterback in a format that starts two, and he responded to that by drafting a fourth running back. Rhamondre Stevenson started thirteen of fourteen games last season and was still out-touched by a rookie at 25.1 percent, which is the kind of man you take when the other position has stopped occurring to you. The team name is still "Waiting to draft...", and at this point it reads less like an oversight than a warning.

James drafted TreVeyon Henderson, who spent last season in a New England committee splitting work with Rhamondre Stevenson, taken three picks earlier by somebody else. So James now owns half of a backfield and Evan owns the other half, which means one of them is right and neither of them knows which. The memories keep getting more expensive.

Colin, a man who has spent this draft walking past the board like it owed him money, took Mark Andrews at the exact moment he was the best player alive. No solo expedition, no twenty-five-pick head start, nobody left behind. We are logging this as a navigational error that happened to land on the runway.
Round 8 and Bree still has 1 quarterback in a superflex league. Bold.

Chenell now has four running backs, three receivers, one tight end and zero quarterbacks in a format that starts two of them. She is defending a title with a roster that cannot legally take a snap. The scoops were real, the news was true, and nobody in the group chat thought to mention the part where somebody has to throw the ball.

Jay, the man who ratified Jonathan Taylor, has finally deviated from consensus, and he chose to do it by taking Marvin Harrison Jr. three spots after Isaiah Likely was still sitting there. The one time he went off-script it was to pay a national price for a local ranking. Independence looks worse on him than obedience did.

James took Michael Wilson while T.J. Hockenson and twenty-six better men sat unclaimed, and the only visible logic is that Wilson catches passes in Arizona, where Marvin Harrison Jr. also works, except Harrison belongs to Jay. So James is not even stacking an offense, he is stacking someone else's. The memories are no longer his own.

Jay has one quarterback, in a format that starts two, and has spent his last five picks on receivers he does not need. Josh Jacobs was available and Jay chose a fifth wideout, which means the only way this roster fields a legal lineup is if the commissioner takes pity. The consensus board he used to ratify has stopped taking his calls.

Bree took Aaron Jones Sr. with literally nobody better left on the board, which for a woman whose entire draft has been a petition to the rest of the league is genuinely disorienting. This required no cooperation from anyone. Three tight ends, one quarterback, and one pick that accidentally did not need permission.

Michael Pittman Jr. joins a roster of four running backs, four receivers, one tight end and the same lonely quarterback, and Chenell paid twenty-seven picks over his national price to get him there. The scoop era, the medical-optimism era, and now the era of simply refusing to acknowledge that half the lineup is illegal. Da Reigning Champ is not defending a title, she is filing an appeal.

Doug walked past Josh Jacobs to take Stefon Diggs, which is the first time in this draft he has walked past a running back at all, and he chose the one moment where taking the running back was correct. He now has six backs and two receivers, so Diggs arrives as the second man in a room built for eight. That roster page he keeps scrolling sideways has developed a horizontal scrollbar of its own.

Three quarterbacks, five running backs, two receivers. Jesse has now assembled a roster where the only legal Sunday lineup involves a quarterback lining up at wideout and a running back explaining the situation to the officials. Mr. Anderson stopped drafting a team several rounds ago and started collecting one position at a time, alphabetically.

That is Doug's seventh running back. He passed on Kenny Gainwell, who would have been an eighth, purely for variety. The relay team has become a marching band, and the two receivers have started asking whether they were traded without being told.

Chenell has now taken a fifth running back while the quarterback column remains a single, terrified name. She has more backs than a superflex lineup has starting slots for humans, and she still needs a second passer more than she needs a Kenny Gainwell. The group chat has gone quiet, mostly out of respect.

Bree took the best player available for the second time tonight, and this one she got eleven picks cheaper than the country would have charged her. Her draft required thirty strangers to underperform; it did not require this, and yet here it is. Two accidents in a row is no longer an accident, it is a condition.

Jay took Evan Engram forty-four picks before the rest of America was going to, having previously been unable to draft a man without checking what everyone else thought first. He passed thirty-one better players to do it, including Brian Thomas Jr., and he still has one quarterback in a format that starts two. The consensus board did not stop taking his calls; it changed its number.

James took MarShawn Lloyd while Brian Thomas Jr., twenty-nine spots better, sat there being an actual first-round talent nobody wanted. That is a fourth running back on a roster with one quarterback, purchased on the same fumes as everything else. The memories have now outrun the film entirely.

Justin took Brian Thomas Jr., the best man on the board, one pick after James went out of his way not to. That is two correct picks in a row, which means the guessing era ended and something worse has replaced it: competence with no explanation. Two quarterbacks, two running backs, five receivers, and Substation Superstars now winning arguments they did not know they were in.

Jordan Addison was genuinely the best man left, so James has finally bought something with cash instead of memories. It gives him one quarterback, four running backs, six receivers and a tight end, which is a roster shaped like a man who has never once looked at the left-hand column. The film has caught up; the lineup card never will.

Colin took Jerry Jeudy twenty-six better players early, which puts the solo expedition back in the field after one brief night at base camp. Quentin Johnston, Cam Ward and Khalil Shakir all watched him walk off into the treeline again. He has three tight ends and three receivers, and Mark Andrews now looks like the accident everyone said he was.

Quentin Johnston was sitting there and Tyler took Wan'Dale Robinson instead, which is the fourth receiver in his last five picks and the sixth overall. He has one running back. The collection is complete enough to tour, and the supply run never happened.

That is Jay's sixth receiver, four of them in his last five picks, and he still has exactly one quarterback in a format that starts two. Calvin Ridley cost him twenty-six better players, including a Cam Ward who plays the position Jay has decided not to believe in. He is no longer drafting a team, he is curating the largest collection of men who cannot throw.

Khalil Shakir was the best man on the board, so Keshia has now been correct twice, both times while standing in an aisle she wandered into for other reasons. He is the fourth receiver in her last five picks, which means she has stopped hoarding quarterbacks and started hoarding the men who catch from them. Five quarterbacks and two receivers before tonight; the darts are now hitting a different wall entirely.

Doug reached twenty-nine spots for Jalen Nailor, walking past Gunnar Helm, Chig Okonkwo and De'Zhaun Stribling to do it, which is the first ambitious thing he has done that did not involve a running back. Nobody in America was taking Nailor here; Doug went and got him anyway. The marching band has hired a soloist and given him a piece nobody wrote.

Chris Godwin Jr. sat there twenty-two spots better while James took Oronde Gadsden, a tight end, on a roster that still has one quarterback. Deebo Samuel Sr. was also available, which means James walked past two men who have actually caught NFL passes to buy a third who might. The memories have stopped being about football and are now purely about James.

Deebo Samuel Sr. was the best man left, so Evan has again succeeded by remaining seated at the right moment. Two quarterbacks, three running backs, five receivers, three tight ends: a roster that starts nine and owns thirteen, most of them stacked in the two positions with the fewest slots. The team name is still "Waiting to draft...", and it is starting to sound like a lifestyle.

Evan took the Broncos defense in round fourteen, having passed on Romeo Doubs, RJ Harvey and Zach Charbonnet, which is the loudest thing he has done all night by a distance of seven hundred and ninety players. This is the first defense off the board, so for one pick Evan was the most decisive man in the league. He waited fourteen rounds to draft, then drafted eleven guys at once.

James answered the one-quarterback problem by drafting the Seattle defense, which contains no quarterbacks and cannot be started at the position either. Romeo Doubs was there. Seven hundred and ninety-one men were there. James looked at a lineup card missing a passer and chose an entire unit whose job is stopping them.

Colin walked past Romeo Doubs, RJ Harvey and Zach Charbonnet to take the Rams defense, which is the solo expedition finally reaching terrain with no players on it at all. Seven hundred and ninety-one better men were standing behind him waving. He did not turn around; he never does.

Jay has one quarterback and now two defenses' worth of men whose entire job description is hitting quarterbacks. The Lions unit arrives to a roster of six receivers and a single passer, so the collection has expanded from men who cannot throw to men who actively prevent throwing. He is curating against his own lineup card at this point.

Bree took the Eagles defense with Romeo Doubs sitting there, and she still has one quarterback in a format that starts two. Her draft has always required thirty strangers to cooperate; it now requires the commissioner to accept eleven Philadelphians under center. The two accidents were the whole run of good luck, and it is over.

Jesse now owns three quarterbacks, six running backs and the Chargers defense, which means he has cornered the market on passers and also on the people paid to flatten them. Romeo Doubs was available; Jesse wanted the jerseys. Mr. Anderson has stopped drafting positions alphabetically and started drafting by team gift shop.

For Brandon Aubrey here to work, Jesse needs the league to add a second kicker slot, needs three quarterbacks to be a legal formation, and needs Romeo Doubs to have been a clerical illusion. This is the first kicker off the board, taken eighty-three picks ahead of where the country had him. The board did not owe him money after all; he just handed it some.

Doug took Cameron Dicker with Romeo Doubs still on the board, which means the marching band now has a man whose only job is a single note from forty yards. Seven backs, four receivers, one soloist, and now a placekicker. The horizontal scrollbar has reached the part of the page where nobody catches anything.

For Jason Myers to matter, Chenell needs the Seahawks to stall inside the thirty every week, needs her one quarterback to survive sixteen games unaccompanied, and needs Romeo Doubs to have been someone else's problem. The appeal has now added a kicker as a character witness. The group chat remains silent.

Bree answered a one-quarterback roster by drafting a man who is not allowed to touch the ball with his hands. Four tight ends, one passer, and now Ka'imi Fairbairn, taken forty-seven picks before the country would have bothered. The petition to the rest of the league has quietly become a petition to the rulebook.

Eddy Pineiro joins six receivers, one quarterback and a defense, which means Jay has now spent five straight picks avoiding the only position his lineup legally requires. Romeo Doubs was there, not that Jay wanted another one of those either. The consensus board changed its number, then moved, then stopped forwarding mail.

James has one quarterback, and his solution tonight has been a defense and now a kicker, neither of which may be listed under center. Jake Bates cost him Romeo Doubs, which at this point is a rounding error against the men he has passed for the sake of not having a second passer. The memories are now being kicked from forty-two yards out.
